### `POST /api/auth/login` { #post-api-auth-login }

Verify credentials, set the session cookie. Accepts form or JSON.

Access: open.

### `POST /api/auth/logout` { #post-api-auth-logout }

Access: open.

### `GET /api/auth/session-status` { #get-api-auth-session-status }

Why a login ended. No auth: it's asked by a page that just got a 401.

``sid`` is the login id the page saved at login time; it is a random
secret only that browser holds. If the record says the login is still
open but the browser has stopped presenting it, it is ended here with the
reason that fits (idle past the cookie lifetime = expired, else the
browser dropped it), so the audit trail has it too.

Access: open.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sid` | query | string | no |

### `POST /api/auth/password` { #post-api-auth-password }

Change your own password. Your other logins end; this one stays.

Access: open.

Request body (`application/json`): **PasswordChange**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `current_password` | string | yes |  |
| `new_password` | string | yes |  |

### `GET /api/auth/me` { #get-api-auth-me }

Access: open.

### `GET /api/auth/sessions` { #get-api-auth-sessions }

Logins, most recently active first. ``active=true`` = still open.

Access: admin role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `active` | query | boolean | no |
| `limit` | query | integer | no |

### `POST /api/auth/sessions/{sid}/revoke` { #post-api-auth-sessions-sid-revoke }

End one login now; its page shows "An administrator ended this login".

Access: admin role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sid` | path | string | yes |

### `GET /api/auth/events` { #get-api-auth-events }

Audit trail: logins, failed logins, logouts, logins ended (newest first).

``username`` (as typed at sign-in, any case) and ``event`` narrow it.

Access: admin role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | query | integer | no |
| `username` | query | string | no |
| `event` | query | string | no |

### `GET /api/metrics` { #get-api-metrics }

Return power time-series for the dashboard chart.

Supports two modes:
- **Relative range**: ``?range=30m`` (default) — last N from now.
- **Absolute date range**: ``?start=<epoch>&end=<epoch>`` — historical query.

Optional ``?bucket=5m`` downsamples to the given interval.
Valid buckets: 1m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m, 1h.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `range` | query | string or null | no |
| `start` | query | number or null | no |
| `end` | query | number or null | no |
| `bucket` | query | string or null | no |
| `gateway_id` | query | string or null | no |

### `GET /api/stats/storage` { #get-api-stats-storage }

Return DB storage statistics (row counts, sizes, time ranges).

Access: any signed-in role.

### `POST /api/metrics/archive` { #post-api-metrics-archive }

Manually trigger metrics archival (downsample old raw data).

Access: admin role.

### `GET /api/alarm-events` { #get-api-alarm-events }

Return alarm events in a time window.

Provide either ``start``+``end`` (Unix timestamps) or ``range``
(e.g. ``30m``, ``1h``, ``24h``).  Events are sparse — only rows
written on register state changes are returned.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | query | number or null | no |
| `end` | query | number or null | no |
| `range` | query | string or null | no |
| `gateway_id` | query | string or null | no |

### `GET /api/events` { #get-api-events }

Return durationed alarm + PV-Clipping events in a time window.

Unlike ``/alarm-events`` (raw SET/CLR transitions), this pairs each
transition into a single row with a start time, end time, and
duration, and merges in PV-Clipping/Grid-Forming intervals derived
from ``metrics.grid_mode``. Same ``start``+``end`` / ``range`` params
as ``/alarm-events``.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | query | number or null | no |
| `end` | query | number or null | no |
| `range` | query | string or null | no |
| `gateway_id` | query | string or null | no |

### `GET /api/settings/metrics` { #get-api-settings-metrics }

Read metrics retention + raw-resolution config.

Access: any signed-in role.

### `PUT /api/settings/metrics` { #put-api-settings-metrics }

Update metrics retention and/or the raw full-resolution window.

raw_age_days is how long full-resolution samples are kept before being
downsampled to 5-min buckets; it must be >= 1 and <= retention_days
(keeping raw longer than total retention is meaningless).

Access: admin role.

Request body (`application/json`): **MetricsSettingsUpdate**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `retention_days` | integer or null | no |  |
| `raw_age_days` | integer or null | no |  |

### `POST /api/sequence/execute` { #post-api-sequence-execute }

Execute a SunSpec Modbus sequence against one or all gateways.

It writes real registers (WSetEna/WSetPct included, i.e. a battery
dispatch), so it needs the ``control`` capability, and every run is
recorded in the control log with who ran it and what it wrote.

Access: `control` capability.

Request body (`application/json`): **SequenceExecRequest**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | list of object or null | no |  |
| `inline` | string or null | no |  |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | false |
| `gateway_id` | string or null | no |  |

### `GET /api/mqtt/config` { #get-api-mqtt-config }

The stored config, plus where each broker field in use comes from (#103).

``sources`` maps host/port/username/password to ``environment`` /
``settings`` / ``supervisor`` / ``default``; ``env_vars`` names the variable
for each field the environment sets, so the form can say why it's locked.

Access: any signed-in role.

### `PATCH /api/mqtt/config` { #patch-api-mqtt-config }

Access: admin role.

Request body (`application/json`): **MqttConfigUpdate**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | string or null | no |  |
| `port` | integer or null | no |  |
| `username` | string or null | no |  |
| `password` | string or null | no |  |
| `tls_mode` | string or null | no |  |
| `enabled` | boolean or null | no |  |
| `client_id` | string or null | no |  |
| `qos` | integer or null | no |  |
| `retain_discovery` | boolean or null | no |  |
| `topic_prefix` | string or null | no |  |
| `discovery_prefix` | string or null | no |  |

### `GET /api/mqtt/namespace` { #get-api-mqtt-namespace }

The namespace in use, the choices, and whether a change needs confirming.

Access: any signed-in role.

### `POST /api/mqtt/namespace` { #post-api-mqtt-namespace }

Change this bridge's MQTT namespace (#87). Admin-only (router gate).

Before anything is published it simply switches. After, ``confirm`` is
required: the old namespace's retained discovery configs that THIS bridge
wrote are removed (another producer's are left), then everything is
republished under the new one. The answer carries the counts.

Access: admin role.

Request body (`application/json`): **NamespaceChange**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `topic_prefix` | string | yes |  |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | false |

### `GET /api/system/timezone` { #get-api-system-timezone }

Detected timezone, whether a user ever confirmed it, and the local time
right now — so the prompt can show what the bridge believes rather than
asking the user to take it on trust.

Access: any signed-in role.

### `POST /api/system/timezone/confirm` { #post-api-system-timezone-confirm }

Record the user's decision, optionally correcting the timezone.

Correcting it here only changes what the bridge EXPECTS. The clock itself
comes from the container, so a correction must also be applied there (TZ in
docker-compose, or the Supervisor's setting) — otherwise the next start
reports a mismatch, which is the honest outcome rather than a silent
disagreement.

Access: admin role.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `timezone` | string or null | no |  |

### `POST /api/services/{service_id}/switch-plan` { #post-api-services-service-id-switch-plan }

Close the current billing period and begin a new plan.

Totals reset at this boundary deliberately: a period must never span two
price sets, or its cost is an average of tariffs that were never both in
force. Closed periods keep their own snapshot of retailer/network/version,
so history reads as what it was.

Access: admin role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service_id` | path | string | yes |

Request body (`application/json`): **PlanSwitch**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `retailer` | string or null | no |  |
| `network` | string or null | no |  |

Export a service's tariff as a portable profile.

Identifying fields are stripped: sharing a plan should not share a meter
number, an account, or a network approval that belongs to one connection.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service_id` | path | string | yes |

### `POST /api/services/import` { #post-api-services-import }

Validate a tariff profile, and optionally apply it.

``dry_run=true`` (the default) reports what would happen without touching
anything — importing a tariff overwrites rates that price real money, so it
should never be a single unconfirmed click.

With ``service_id`` the profile is applied to that service, leaving its
identity and network grant intact. Without one, a new service is created.

Access: admin role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dry_run` | query | boolean | no |
| `service_id` | query | string or null | no |

Request body (`application/json`): **TariffImportBundle**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string or null | no |  |
| `version` | integer or null | no |  |
| `exported_at` | number or null | no |  |
| `profile` | object | no |  |

### `POST /api/gateways/{gw_id}/start` { #post-api-gateways-gw-id-start }

| `gw_id` | path | string | yes |

### `POST /api/gateways/{gw_id}/stop` { #post-api-gateways-gw-id-stop }

Stop polling a gateway and remember the stop across restarts.

Sets ``autostart=0`` so the gateway is not re-started on the next app
boot.  ``enabled`` stays 1 — this is a user pause, not an admin disable,
so the gateway remains configured and can be started again.  This is what
keeps a stopped (esp. mock) gateway from self-restarting on reboot.

Access: admin role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gw_id` | path | string | yes |

### `POST /api/gateways/{gw_id}/restart` { #post-api-gateways-gw-id-restart }

Tear down and recreate a gateway's Modbus connection.

Unlike /diagnose (read-only), this is the actual fix for a wedged
session: it discards the current GatewayInstance (closing whatever
socket state it had, good or bad) and reconnects from scratch, without
needing a full bridge process restart. ``registry.start_gateway``
already stops any existing instance for this ID before starting a new
one, so this is mechanically identical to /start — this endpoint exists
for a clear, explicit "restart" action in the UI/CLI regardless of
whether the gateway looked like it was already running.

Access: admin role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gw_id` | path | string | yes |

### `POST /api/gateways/{gw_id}/healthcheck` { #post-api-gateways-gw-id-healthcheck }

Force an immediate TCP health probe, instead of waiting for the
periodic HealthChecker (default: every 60s) to get to this gateway.

Updates the same ``status.health`` field the topbar dot reads, so the
UI reflects the result on its next refresh.

Access: admin role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gw_id` | path | string | yes |

### `GET /api/gateways/{gw_id}/detect-phases` { #get-api-gateways-gw-id-detect-phases }

Auto-detect the gateway's wired phase(s) from its 701 registers.

Reads the gateway's latest cached points (no extra Modbus traffic) and
infers connected/utilised phases. Also reports whether the result matches
the gateway's currently declared ``phase``.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gw_id` | path | string | yes |

### `POST /api/gateways/{gw_id}/test` { #post-api-gateways-gw-id-test }

Test TCP connectivity to a gateway's host:port.

Access: admin role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gw_id` | path | string | yes |

### `POST /api/gateways/{gw_id}/diagnose` { #post-api-gateways-gw-id-diagnose }

Root-cause a Modbus connectivity problem for a gateway.

Runs TCP reachability probes (Modbus port + Local API port), a live
Modbus protocol-level read reusing the poller's existing session (never
opens a second concurrent Modbus session — see docs/vendor-issues.md on
concurrent-access corruption), and cross-checks the result against the
poller's own reported state to catch cases where the poller thinks it's
fine but isn't.

Access: admin role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gw_id` | path | string | yes |

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |

### `GET /api/gateways/{gw_id}/battery/limits` { #get-api-gateways-gw-id-battery-limits }

Battery power limits a force command may use: trusted ratings only (#133).

``max_charge_w`` / ``max_discharge_w`` are None until the rating is
calibrated or Model 702 is confirmed by an observed peak; no 5000 W default.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gw_id` | path | string | yes |

### `GET /api/gateways/{gw_id}/battery-rating` { #get-api-gateways-gw-id-battery-rating }

The evidence behind this gateway's battery power rating, per direction (#133).

``trusted`` says whether force commands are allowed; ``reason`` says why
not and how to fix it. ``calibration`` is the window being recorded, if any.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gw_id` | path | string | yes |

### `POST /api/gateways/{gw_id}/battery-rating/calibration` { #post-api-gateways-gw-id-battery-rating-calibration }

Record the battery's full-rate power while the owner runs a dispatch in the app.

Start, then in the FranklinWH app run a TOU battery dispatch (force charge
from grid, or force discharge to grid) with import and export unlimited, at
mid SoC. Finish after at least a minute: the peak becomes the calibrated
rating for that direction. The bridge sends nothing to the aGate here.

Access: `control` capability.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gw_id` | path | string | yes |

Request body (`application/json`): **CalibrationRequest**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | yes |  |
| `direction` | string or null | no |  |

### `GET /api/gateways/{gw_id}/dispatch-outcomes` { #get-api-gateways-gw-id-dispatch-outcomes }

Every battery command sent to this gateway and how it ended, newest first.

States: sent / failed / verified / not_effective / reasserted / released /
release_unverified / superseded (design PR #57 §5.1). ``requester`` says
who asked: ``schedule:<entry id>`` or ``manual``.

Access: any signed-in role.

### `GET /api/setup/state` { #get-api-setup-state }

Whether the wizard should open. Any signed-in user may ask; only admins
are shown the wizard (the UI checks the role).

### `POST /api/setup/state` { #post-api-setup-state }

Record a choice — typically ``skipped``, or ``pending`` to run it again.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | string | yes |  |

### `GET /api/setup/subnets` { #get-api-setup-subnets }

Subnets to search, each with where it came from (see environment.py).

Also the networks of aGates already set up here: an aGate reached over
Tailscale or a VPN lives on a network the bridge's host isn't on, so the
host's own interfaces never suggest it — but a second aGate is usually on
the same network as the first.

Access: admin role.

### `POST /api/setup/scan` { #post-api-setup-scan }

Search subnets for aGates in the background; poll ``GET /scan/{id}``.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |

| `subnets` | list of string | yes |  |
| `port` | integer | no | 502 |

Access: admin role.

|---|---|---|---|
| `scan_id` | path | string | yes |

### `POST /api/setup/probe` { #post-api-setup-probe }

Identify one address (the wizard's *Enter address → Test*).

Access: admin role.

Request body (`application/json`): **ProbeRequest**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | string | yes |  |
| `port` | integer | no | 502 |
| `unit_id` | integer | no | 1 |

### `POST /api/setup/connect` { #post-api-setup-connect }

Set up a real gateway at this address and start it.

The first one fills the primary gateway (internally still id ``default``,
which owns the unprefixed MQTT topics existing HA setups rely on); any
further ones are added alongside.

Access: admin role.

Request body (`application/json`): **ConnectRequest**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `host` | string | yes |  |
| `port` | integer | no | 502 |
| `unit_id` | integer | no | 1 |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `device_type` | string | no | "agate" |

### `POST /api/setup/demo` { #post-api-setup-demo }

Create a demo (mock) gateway.

Always a separate gateway — never the primary: the primary owns the
unprefixed MQTT topics, and synthetic data there would land in the same HA
entities (and long-term statistics) a real aGate uses later.

Not published to Home Assistant until the user says so (#96): as an add-on
a demo used to put a "Demo aGate" device into the user's real HA unasked.

Access: admin role.

Request body (`application/json`): **DemoRequest**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | no | "Demo aGate" |
| `ac_type` | integer | no | 0 |

### `POST /api/setup/use-ha` { #post-api-setup-use-ha }

Record whether this install is used with Home Assistant (#94).

Not asked as an add-on, which always runs inside Home Assistant.

Access: admin role.

Request body (`application/json`): **UseHaUpdate**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `use_ha` | boolean | yes |  |

### `POST /api/setup/publish-to-ha` { #post-api-setup-publish-to-ha }

The wizard's "Publish <gateway>'s entities to Home Assistant?" (#96).

The same switch as ``PATCH /api/gateways/{id}`` ``publish_to_ha``, and
applied the same way — live: off removes the entities from HA, on
publishes them. Returns the checklist, which reflects the answer.

Access: admin role.

Request body (`application/json`): **PublishToHaUpdate**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gateway_id` | string | yes |  |
| `publish` | boolean | yes |  |

### `GET /api/setup/checklist` { #get-api-setup-checklist }

Step 6: is everything between the bridge and Home Assistant working?

Each item is ``ok`` / ``fail`` / ``unknown`` (couldn't tell — shown as a
manual step) / ``skipped`` (not using Home Assistant), with a ``detail``.

Access: admin role.

### `GET /api/setup/accounts` { #get-api-setup-accounts }

Logins on this bridge, and which still have a password anyone would
try first ("admin", the username...). The shipped compose seeds
admin/admin, so a new install starts there.

Under HA ingress the bridge's own logins aren't used: ``applies`` is false.

Access: admin role.

## Energy

| Method | Path | Summary | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | [`/api/energy/flow`](#get-api-energy-flow) | Energy Flow | any signed-in role |
| `GET` | [`/api/energy/battery-hours`](#get-api-energy-battery-hours) | Battery Hours | any signed-in role |
| `GET` | [`/api/energy/totals`](#get-api-energy-totals) | Energy Totals Endpoint | any signed-in role |

### `GET /api/energy/flow` { #get-api-energy-flow }

Directional energy flows for a day (default today) or an explicit span.

``day`` is the common case and what the dashboards use. ``start``/``end``
epoch seconds cover week/month/year views without a second endpoint.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `day` | query | string or null | no |
| `start` | query | number or null | no |
| `end` | query | number or null | no |
| `gateway` | query | string | no |

### `GET /api/energy/battery-hours` { #get-api-energy-battery-hours }

Per-hour battery charge/discharge for a local day (default today).

Feeds the Solar Forecast card's charging/discharging band. Integrated from
the sampled ``battery_w`` series (sign-split, so a mixed hour reports both
directions) — an estimate from sampled power, not a meter reading.
Hours after now carry ``state: null``.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `day` | query | string or null | no |
| `gateway` | query | string | no |

### `GET /api/energy/totals` { #get-api-energy-totals }

Lifetime and period kWh, straight from the aGate's own counters.

Measured, not reconstructed — these are the figures to trust when they
disagree with the Sankey's arcs.

Projected out of the same sensor snapshot the Automation Builder and the
schedule engine read, rather than re-deriving the counters here. A second
derivation is a second thing to drift: the whole point of these being the
trustworthy numbers is that there is exactly one of them.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gateway` | query | string | no |

Current recording settings, plus the catalogue a client can offer.

Access: any signed-in role.

### `PUT /api/point-history/config` { #put-api-point-history-config }

Update recording settings.

Takes effect on the next poll tick — the loop re-reads this each pass rather
than caching it, so there is nothing to restart. Shrinking retention does
not delete anything here; the purge pass applies it on its own schedule.

Access: `control` capability.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean or null | no |  |
| `points` | list of string or null | no |  |
| `interval_s` | integer or null | no |  |
| `retention_days` | integer or null | no |  |

### `GET /api/point-history/series` { #get-api-point-history-series }

Historical series for a comma-separated ``points`` list.

``bucket_s`` is chosen automatically from the span unless given. The
response echoes the resolved span and bucket so a caller can label the
axis with what it actually got rather than what it asked for.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `points` | query | string | yes |
| `day` | query | string or null | no |
| `start` | query | number or null | no |
| `end` | query | number or null | no |
| `bucket_s` | query | number or null | no |
| `gateway` | query | string | no |

### `GET /api/point-history/storage` { #get-api-point-history-storage }

What point history costs now, and what a candidate config would cost.

The projection query params let Settings show the consequence of a change
while the user is still deciding, without saving it first.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `points` | query | integer or null | no |
| `interval_s` | query | number or null | no |
| `retention_days` | query | number or null | no |

Live wholesale price: the AEMO NEM spot for ``region`` (default: the
configured one) and the configured HA price entities, plus the ACTIVE
buy/sell (HA wins per side over NEM). No region and nothing configured ->
``spot: null``, and nothing is fetched.

| `region` | query | string or null | no |
| `force` | query | boolean | no |

NEM region + HA price entities, for the Settings form.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nem_region` | string or null | no |  |
| `tariff_price_entity` | string or null | no |  |
| `tariff_feedin_entity` | string or null | no |  |

### `GET /api/tariff/dynamic` { #get-api-tariff-dynamic }

The live price a dynamic plan is (or would be) priced at.

With no ``source``: the ACTIVE plan's provider and the live price billing
is using now (``live`` is null for a static plan). With ``source`` (``nem``
+ ``region``, or ``ha`` + ``buy_entity`` [+ ``feedin_entity``]): a preview
for the tariff editor, before anything is saved. Invalid input -> 422.

Access: any signed-in role.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |

| `source` | query | string or null | no |

| `buy_entity` | query | string or null | no |

Closed billing periods (reporting/history), most-recent first.

| `priority` | integer | no | 0 |
| `trigger_kind` | string or null | no |  |

| `exit_conditions` | object or null | no |  |

### `GET /api/schedules/export` { #get-api-schedules-export }

Export schedules as a portable JSON bundle. ``ids`` = comma-separated
entry ids (default: all).

Access: any signed-in role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | query | string or null | no |

### `POST /api/schedules/import` { #post-api-schedules-import }

Validate (and optionally create) an imported bundle. ``dry_run=true``
(default) returns a per-entry validation report without creating anything;
``dry_run=false`` creates the valid entries DISABLED (for review), with any
unknown gateway target falling back to Default.

Access: admin role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dry_run` | query | boolean | no |

Request body (`application/json`): **ImportBundle**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string or null | no |  |
| `version` | integer or null | no |  |
| `entries` | list of object | no |  |

### `GET /api/schedules/log` { #get-api-schedules-log }

Recent schedule dispatch/audit events (newest first).

Optional filters: ``schedule_id`` (one entry's runs) and ``status`` (the
audit result: fired/gated/missed/executed/exit_condition_met/…) — this backs
the FWHAI audit + history views.

Access: any signed-in role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | query | integer | no |
| `schedule_id` | query | string or null | no |
| `status` | query | string or null | no |

### `POST /api/schedules/{schedule_id}/execute` { #post-api-schedules-schedule-id-execute }

Fire a schedule entry's action now (respects entry_conditions unless
``?force=true``). The dispatch auto-releases after the entry's duration.

Access: admin role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schedule_id` | path | string | yes |
| `force` | query | boolean | no |

### `POST /api/schedules/{schedule_id}/stop` { #post-api-schedules-schedule-id-stop }

Gracefully stop a schedule's CURRENT run: release the live dispatch it
owns and skip re-firing until the next scheduled window. The entry stays
enabled (disable it to stop permanently).

Access: admin role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schedule_id` | path | string | yes |

### `GET /api/schedules/timeline` { #get-api-schedules-timeline }

Return the day's windows per entry for the visual timeline.

``day`` is an optional weekday (0=Mon..6=Sun) to preview; defaults to today.
Each segment is minutes-from-midnight so the UI can lay out a 24h bar.

Access: any signed-in role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `day` | query | integer or null | no |

### `GET /api/schedules/{schedule_id}` { #get-api-schedules-schedule-id }

Get one schedule entry.

Access: any signed-in role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schedule_id` | path | string | yes |

### `PATCH /api/schedules/{schedule_id}` { #patch-api-schedules-schedule-id }

Update a schedule entry.

Uses ``exclude_unset`` so we apply exactly the fields the client sent —
including explicit nulls. A previous ``if v is not None`` filter silently
dropped nulls, which made it impossible to CLEAR a field: deleting all
exit_conditions (client sends ``exit_conditions: null``) never persisted.
``update_schedule`` stores None as SQL NULL for the nullable JSON columns.

Access: admin role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schedule_id` | path | string | yes |

Request body (`application/json`): **ScheduleUpdate**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string or null | no |  |
| `when_spec` | WhenSpec or null | no |  |
| `action` | string or null | no |  |
| `params` | object or null | no |  |
| `target_type` | string or null | no |  |
| `target_id` | string or null | no |  |
| `enabled` | boolean or null | no |  |
| `release` | string or null | no |  |
| `conflict` | string or null | no |  |
| `priority` | integer or null | no |  |
| `trigger_kind` | string or null | no |  |
| `trigger_spec` | object or null | no |  |
| `entry_conditions` | object or null | no |  |
| `exit_conditions` | object or null | no |  |
| `duration_s` | integer or null | no |  |
| `release_policy` | string or null | no |  |
| `missed_policy` | string or null | no |  |
| `entry_hold_s` | integer or null | no |  |
| `ha_actions` | list of HaActionItem or null | no |  |

### `DELETE /api/schedules/{schedule_id}` { #delete-api-schedules-schedule-id }

Delete a schedule entry.

Access: admin role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schedule_id` | path | string | yes |

The command vocabulary a schedule entry can dispatch (for the UI form).

Access: any signed-in role; module `automations`.

### `GET /api/sensors` { #get-api-sensors }

Sensor namespace + current values for the condition-builder dropdowns.

Includes the static Bridge sensors plus any HA entities (``ha:<inst>:<entity>``)
so the Automation Builder can condition on Home Assistant state.

Access: any signed-in role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gateway` | query | string | no |

### `GET /api/automation/constants` { #get-api-automation-constants }

User-defined automation constants (min/max/demand SoC) + their [min,max]
bounds for the settings form. Surfaced as ``const.*`` sensors too.

Access: any signed-in role; module `automations`.

### `PUT /api/automation/constants` { #put-api-automation-constants }

Update automation constants (only sent fields; each clamped to [0,100]).

Access: admin role; module `automations`.

| Field | Type | Required | Default |

Evaluate a condition tree against the gateway's live snapshot.

result}]}`` — the Test Verification response.

Access: admin role; module `automations`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gateway` | query | string | no |

Request body (`application/json`): **ConditionTreeBody**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match` | string | no | "ALL" |
| `conditions` | list of object | no |  |

### `POST /api/ha/test` { #post-api-ha-test }

Probe a base_url/token WITHOUT saving — powers the config form's Test button.

On an edit the token field is blank; if ``ha_id`` is given we fall back to
that instance's stored token so Test reflects the real (saved) credentials
instead of failing 401 with no auth.

Returns ``{connected, entity_count, last_error}``.

Access: admin role; module `ha_entities`.

Request body (`application/json`): **HaTestBody**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | string | yes |  |
| `token` | string or null | no |  |
| `ha_id` | string or null | no |  |

### `GET /api/ha/notify-targets` { #get-api-ha-notify-targets }

Available ``notify.*`` services across all HA instances.

Notify targets are services, not entities, so they never appear in the
entity browser — the action picker needs them from here.

Access: any signed-in role; module `ha_entities`.

### `GET /api/ha/entities` { #get-api-ha-entities }

Browse ALL HA entities across instances (with an ``exposed`` flag),
filtered + paginated — backs the HA Entities tab.

Filters: ``instance`` (id), ``domain``, ``search`` (substring of entity_id or
friendly name), ``exposed`` (true/false). Returns
``{total, page, page_size, exposed_count, entities:[...]}``.

``search`` accepts **comma-separated terms matched as OR** — real
installations name the same concept a dozen ways ("pv", "solar",
"enphase", "envoy"), so a single substring misses most of a topic. A
plain term without commas behaves exactly as before.

Access: any signed-in role; module `ha_entities`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `instance` | query | string or null | no |
| `domain` | query | string or null | no |
| `search` | query | string or null | no |
| `exposed` | query | boolean or null | no |
| `page` | query | integer | no |
| `page_size` | query | integer | no |

### `GET /api/ha/domains` { #get-api-ha-domains }

Distinct entity domains across all instances (for the filter dropdown).

Access: any signed-in role; module `ha_entities`.

### `POST /api/ha/entities/expose` { #post-api-ha-entities-expose }

Add/remove an entity from an instance's allowlist (persists + applies live).

Access: admin role; module `ha_entities`.

Request body (`application/json`): **HaExposeBody**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `instance_id` | string | yes |  |
| `entity_id` | string | yes |  |
| `exposed` | boolean | yes |  |

### `GET /api/ha/dashboard-yaml` { #get-api-ha-dashboard-yaml }

Copy-paste HA dashboard card YAML for this bridge's entities (#86).

Entity ids come only from the chosen HA instance's device + entity
registries — never predicted. Returns ``{yaml, entity_count, devices,
instance, layout}``; 409/503 with a ``detail`` (and no YAML) when the
registry can't be read or holds none of our entities.

Access: any signed-in role; module `ha_entities`.

| Parameter | In | Type | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `instance` | query | string or null | no |
| `layout` | query | string | no |
| `diagnostics` | query | boolean | no |


## Web UI and legacy command

| Method | Path | Summary | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | [`/`](#get) | Index | open |
| `GET` | [`/user`](#get-user) | User Dashboard | open |
| `GET` | [`/login`](#get-login) | Login Page | open |
| `POST` | [`/api/command`](#post-api-command) | Send Command | `control` capability |
| `POST` | [`/api/ui/connection-outage`](#post-api-ui-connection-outage) | Report Connection Outage | any signed-in role |

### `GET /` { #get }

Serve the main SPA shell. Unauthenticated → /login; non-admin → /user;
an api account gets the "REST API only" page.

Access: open.

### `GET /user` { #get-user }

The simplified, mobile-first end-user dashboard. Any signed-in role may
view it (admins can preview it here); unauthenticated → /login.

Access: open.

### `GET /login` { #get-login }

The login form. Already-authenticated users go to their role's home.

Access: open.

### `POST /api/command` { #post-api-command }

Dispatch a control command (same path as MQTT commands).

Defaults to the "default" gateway. Use POST /api/gateways/{gw_id}/command
for gateway-specific commands (added in MG-3).

Access: `control` capability.

Request body (`application/json`): **CommandRequest**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slug` | string | yes |  |
| `value` | string | yes |  |

### `POST /api/ui/connection-outage` { #post-api-ui-connection-outage }

Log an outage the browser saw (it couldn't reach the bridge).

Access: any signed-in role.

Request body (`application/json`): **ConnectionOutage**

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `started_at` | number | yes |  |
| `ended_at` | number | yes |  |
| `failures` | integer | no | 0 |
| `message` | string | no |  |
| `url` | string | no |  |
| `device_offline` | boolean | no | false |
| `page` | string | no |  |
